_comment: The gm spec for workflows-in-skills. This repo IS a workflow definition: point a project or a whole user at it and gm runs THIS workflow instead of its compiled defaults. Everything here was extracted from the live rs-plugkit defaults (fsm-vendor generated fsm/graph.json and fsm/predicates.md; prose/*.md are the real compiled instruction sources), so pointing at this repo unmodified reproduces stock gm behaviour exactly -- it is a starting point to edit, not an approximation to drift from.

instructions._comment: Per-state prose. Each key maps to a state's prose_key in fsm/graph.json, plus 'entry' (served every turn, every phase) and 'browser'. crate::prose::resolve picks project-vendored .gm/instructions/<key>.md first, then this repo's cached copy, then the compiled default -- so overriding one key here leaves every other key on its default. This keys list is also what scripts/sync-from-plugkit.mjs iterates when regenerating the snapshot: a compiled key missing from it fails the sync loudly rather than being dropped silently.

fsm._comment: The whole state machine as data: states, edges, the gates guarding each transition, and policy (allowlists, thresholds, terminal phase). Replacing graph.json is how a genuinely different workflow -- different phases, different order, different gates -- is established without touching Rust. gates.predicate may only name a predicate from fsm/predicates.md, which is GENERATED from the same registry the code dispatches on, so a graph cannot silently reference a gate condition that does not exist. A condition outside that registry needs a jit hook (hooks/) instead.

messages._comment: Operator-editable text for gate denials and residual-scan findings, resolved through the same per-key chain as prose. Changing a denial message never changes when the gate fires -- only what the agent is told.

index._comment: Codeinsight/code-index behaviour. Budgets exist because one oversized file must never be able to stall the whole pass or starve the supervisor heartbeat.

memory._comment: The RAG/recall pipeline. embed_dim is load-bearing: changing it invalidates every stored vector, which is why a dim change routes through the explicit drop-if-mismatch path rather than being applied silently to a populated store.

cache._comment: Budgets for the shared cache layer. Per-namespace so one greedy consumer cannot evict another's entries.

sync._comment: How often a repo-backed config tier re-checks its remote. The check is a cheap remote-ref probe; a full fetch only happens when the sha actually moved, so raising the debounce saves bandwidth and lowering it speeds propagation.
